title: Signal pruning and graceful-degradation choreography playbook
author: Claire Nguyen
content:
Overview

Purpose: This playbook defines a cross-cutting contract for telemetry signal pruning (what to sample and why), the safe thresholds that trigger graceful-degradation policies, and the choreography between API clients, edge proxies, and the runtime to enforce low-cost, high-confidence observability during load or degradation events. It combines guidance across API standards, coding patterns, infra controls, model-serving behavior, observability best practices, and a lightweight ADR that captures the decision rationale.

When to use this playbook
- Onboard a new telemetry signal or metric that increases cardinality (new labels, long strings, or unbounded IDs).
- Designing SLO-driven graceful degradation for latency/cost surges.
- Implementing runtime feature flags and client hints for adaptive sampling.
- Auditing telemetry costs during a sustained surge (>48h) or recurring monthly spikes.

Principles
1) Signal intent first: every telemetry field must have an owner, a written intent, and an expiration or retention justification.
2) Minimal stable keys: prefer enumerated labels (finite sets) over free-form strings; free-form data must be hashed and sampled.
3) Degradation as a feature: graceful degradation should be predictable, observable, reversible, and covered by tests and runbooks.
4) Client-aware sampling: allow clients to provide hints (priority, debug=true) but do not trust high-volume clients to change global sampling without rate limits.
5) Cost SLOs: Observability costs are treated as first-class budget items and mapped to product SLO tiers.

Cross-cutting requirements (summary table)
- API contract: request metadata must include telemetry_hint and activity_class (see example).
- Coding: new telemetry fields added in code must include unit tests validating cardinality and a sampling fallback.
- Infra: sampling decisions must be enforceable at the edge (Envoy/edge-proxy) and runtime ingress.
- Model-serving: KV and prompt telemetry must support prefix-hash sampling to avoid exposing prompt details while preserving correlation.
- Observability: metric/trace/event retention and aggregation policies documented in the catalog.
- Performance: sampling logic must add <0.5ms p50 to request routing paths.

Detailed API contract
- New request fields (spec):
  - telemetry_hint (enum: low, normal, high, debug) — optional. High requests counted against quota tiers. Debug forces higher sampling but must be rate-limited server-side.
  - activity_class (enum: interactive, batch, async) — required. Used to select SLO and sampling profile.
  - telemetry_id (string) — optional client-generated opaque id; should be at most 128 characters and hashed by our stack before storage.
- Contract invariants:
  - Servers must never persist raw free-form prompt or user content in telemetry. All string fields labeled as 'sensitive' must be hashed with non-reversible salt.
  - Telemetry sampling decision must be recorded in the request envelope (sampled:true/false) so downstream systems can correlate.

Coding standards and patterns
- New metric/field checklist (PR required):
  1) Owner assigned in the metric catalog.
  2) Purpose statement included in the telemetry annotation.
  3) Cardinality estimate (finite list? high-cardinality?) and proposed sampling rule.
  4) Unit + integration tests: ensure sampling behaves deterministic under a fixed seed; ensure metric emission is idempotent on retries.
  5) Backward compatibility note if removing fields.
- Utility helpers (recommended):
  - telemetry/hash_for_storage(s: string) -> hex128 (salted, server-side only).
  - telemetry/sample(seed, rate) -> boolean (deterministic, seed-based for resampling stability).

Infra standards and enforcement points
- Enforcement layers:
  1) Edge (Envoy filter): enforce max_label_count=12, truncate long labels to 128 chars, and apply client-level sampling caps.
  2) Ingress API gateway: authoritative sampling decision when client hint absent.
  3) Runtime front-tier (router/dispatcher): record decision and attach sampling metadata to downstream calls.
  4) Telemetry pipeline ingestion: final pruning and rollup step; reject samples that violate PII rules.
- Configuration knobs (defaults):
  - global_sampling_rate: 0.05 (5% overall by default)
  - interactive_override: 0.25 (interactive requests higher priority)
  - debug_max_tokens_per_minute: 10 per-key
  - expensive_high_cardinality_rate: 0.005
- Guardrails:
  - Any change to global_sampling_rate or interactive_override requires an infra config rollout with a canary and a commit message referencing this playbook.

Model-serving and KV/prompt telemetry
- Prompt telemetry policy:
  - Never emit raw prompt text in logs/metrics. Emit only hashed prompt-signature and synthetic prompt features (e.g., token_length_bucket).
  - Store prefix KV miss/hit counts with bounded cardinality buckets.
- Model-run performance telemetry:
  - Tokenization latencies and kernel-select decisions can be sampled at 1% unless flagged as anomalous.
  - For end-to-end request traces that include model latency spikes, require a follow-up full-sample flagged for triage (recorded by owners).

Observability design and dashboards
- Dashboard guidance:
  - Low-cost overview panel: sampled-error-rate, sampled-p95-latency, sampled-cost-per-token across priority classes.
  - Degradation incident panel: sampling_rate_changes, telemetry_ingest_backpressure, edge_drop_rate.
  - Signal-quality panel: unique_label_count_by_metric, percent-traces-with-sampled-context.
- Alert rules (suggested):
  1) telemetry_ingest_backpressure > 1m sustained -> P1 on-call paging.
  2) unique_label_count_by_metric > threshold (owner-configured) for 30m -> Ticket to owner.
  3) sampled-error-rate > baseline_error_rate + 2% absolute for 5m -> Notify SRE and product.

Graceful-degradation choreography (orchestration)
- Degrade phases (automated, timeboxed):
  1) Observe: detect cost/latency breach (SLO breach signal).
  2) Prune: edge applies updated sampling profile and strips optional telemetry to reduce ingestion.
  3) Shift: runtime switches to lower-fidelity model variant or reduced output length ceilings.
  4) Backfill: once stable, mark intervals for offline backfills and schedule synthetic-replay evaluations.
- Execution steps (operator-run / automated):
  1) Trigger detection: automated monitor sets 'degradation_event' tag in the alerting system.
  2) Automated action: a pre-authorized policy applies an edge sampling override (API: POST /ops/telemetry/override).
  3) Notify: incident channel populated with current sampling table, affected model variants, and expected impact matrix.
  4) Evaluate: product and SRE approve further steps to shift fidelity; engineering can apply model variant toggles via rollout service.
  5) Recovery: revert sampling override and kick off backfill job.
- Expected impacts table (example):
  - Edge-only prune: ingestion -40%, p95 latency -5%
  - Runtime variant shift: cost -30%, quality (prompt-sensitive tasks) -1-3% MRR-impact risk (product to evaluate)

Runbook snippets
- Quick recovery checklist (for on-call):
  1) Confirm alert: check telemetry_ingest_backpressure and unique_label_count_by_metric.
  2) Apply emergency sampling override (edge) with rate=0.02 for interactive class.
  3) If ingest backlog persists after 3 minutes, apply runtime variant shift to degraded_fidelity_2.
  4) Communicate to product and CS with expected user impact matrix.
  5) After stabilization, schedule backfill and compliance verification.

Config examples
- Edge sampling override payload (JSON example):
  {"override_id": "evt-20260110-01",
    "target": "interactive",
    "new_sampling_rate": "0.02",
    "expiry": "2026-01-10T15:30:00Z",
    "reason": "ingest_backpressure",
    "author": "sre-automation"
  }

- Sampling rules (YAML-like pseudo):
  - name: interactive_high_priority
    match: activity_class == interactive
    rate: 0.25
    max_labels: 8
  - name: default
    match: true
    rate: 0.05
    max_labels: 12
  - name: debug
    match: telemetry_hint == debug
    rate: 1.0
    caps: debug_max_tokens_per_minute

Decision record (ADR summary)
- Problem: Unbounded telemetry cardinality and aggressive sampling during cost surges led to recurring ingestion backpressure and high bills in Q2 2025.
- Options considered:
  A) Continue current practice and rely on post-ingest pruning.
  B) Enforce edge-level pruning + client hints + runtime degradations (this playbook).
  C) Aggressively downsample all telemetry during surge (heavy-handed).
- Decision: Adopt option B. Rationale: preserves useful signals for debugging while controlling cost; allows predictable, testable degradation; supports targeted backfills.
- Consequences: Adds complexity (new infra knobs, more cross-team coordination) but reduces peak ingest costs by expected 35% during surges and prevents data loss for critical traces.

Rollout plan and owner matrix
- Phase 1 (2 weeks): implement edge filter + sampling library; owners: eng-infra (Marcus Li), eng-serving-runtime (Priya Shah). Canary on non-prod with synthetic traffic.
- Phase 2 (3 weeks): instrument dashboards and automated override endpoint; owners: eng-platform (Alan Brooks), observability team.
- Phase 3 (4 weeks): opt-in rollout to 50% production traffic; collect metrics and iterate.
- Final owner (long-term): Observability steward (rotating quarterly), SRE pager for on-call.

Testing and verification
- Unit tests: sampling deterministic behavior; hashing correctness.
- Integration tests: simulate client hints and verify edge/inbound sampling decision aligns with config.
- Load tests: synthetic ingest bursts to validate backpressure and automated override workflows.
- Acceptance criteria: telemetry_ingest_backpressure no longer triggers when simulated load <= 1.5x baseline with sampling rules applied.

Open items and follow-ups
- Define owner for each existing high-cardinality metric in the master catalog (action: measurement sweep, due 2026-02-15).
- Add a standard template for telemetry PRs to reduce friction.
- Formalize cost-to-SLO mapping for degradations in product tiers (product + finance).

Appendix: sample unit test (pseudocode)
- test_sampling_deterministic:
  seed = 42
  rates = [0.05, 0.25, 1.0]
  assert sample(hash(seed, client_id), rates[0]) == false // deterministic under seed
